scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The Garrotín originated in the late 19th century, likely as a northern Spanish folk dance that migrated to Catalonia.
It was developed by Roma communities in Lleida and Barcelona before being integrated into the flamenco repertoire.
It was documented as a theatrical dance by José Otero in 1912.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music is played in a major mode with a 2/4 meter, similar to the tango flamenco.
It is traditionally accompanied by guitar, though piano and orchestral arrangements have been used in the context of the 'copla andaluza'.
Listen for the Guitar, Piano, Orchestra.
The pulse is 2/4.
A major-mode, upbeat flamenco style characterized by a repetitive, rhythmic chorus and humorous, improvised lyrics set to a 2/4 tango-derived beat.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Pastora Pavón (La Niña de los Peines), Carmen Amaya, Faíco, Caetano, Manuel Torre, Pastora Imperio, Antonio Gades, Rafael Riqueni.
Variants are associated with Asturias, León, Valladolid, and the Catalan provinces of Lleida, Tarragona, and Barcelona.
Considered an ancestor of the Catalan rumba; shares a compás with the Farruca and is related to the tango flamenco.
